newsitem.title: RUSSIA: "Clinton is worse than Hitler" Zhirinovsky says.
newsitem.headline: "Clinton is worse than Hitler" Zhirinovsky says.

text.p: Russian ultranationalist Vladimir Zhirinovsky hurled a torrent of abuse at Bill Clinton on Thursday, saying the U.S. president was "worse than Hitler" for launching air strikes against Iraq.

"Napoleon and Hitler are children compared with Clinton. Clinton is worse than Hitler. The U.S. action is bullying on a planetary scale," Zhirinovsky said, calling on Russian pilots to fly to Iraq's defence against this week's U.S. air strikes.

"I have said more than once, that one cannot sit with Clinton at one table for breakfast, lunch or dinner. What America is doing is monstrous, but it is in character because only brigands went to America," he told a news conference.
"For an election victory Clinton is ready to burn a few more capitals," Zhirinovsky said, referring to the U.S. election in November but without mentioning which cities he had in mind.

The outburst showed that Zhirinovsky has not lost the talent to provoke that brought him to the limelight of post-communist Russian politics and sent a shiver of fear through a string of European countries, several of which denied him entry.

In this year's July presidential election he appeared to have run out of steam, coming fifth with just under six percent of the vote, overshadowed by Alexander Lebed, who stole some of his nationalist thunder.

Lebed, now President Boris Yeltsin's national security adviser, on Thursday led Moscow's verbal assault on Washington's action, saying the United States was behaving like a "bull in a china shop" with his air strikes.
Other Russian officials have given more measured, but equally condemning appraisals, with Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov saying the strikes were setting a dangerous precedent.
Not to be outdone, Zhirnovsky, who considers Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein his personal friend and has visited him several times, went a step further.

"There is a hooligan named Bill, and he does whatever he likes. It is banditry and international robbery," he said, adding that Clinton should be named a criminal and taken to the International Court of Human Rights in The Hague.
Zhirinovsky also taunted Yeltsin, saying a "normal" Russian president would have sent a fleet to the Gulf by now and thrown out the U.S. ambassador to Moscow.
He issued a statement in which he called on Russian pilots to fly voluntarily to Iraq to help Baghdad defend itself.

"One need not fear hooligan Bill, a hooligan makes a noise when there is no police force. Russia could be that police force to make Clinton pull up his trousers and run back inside the White House fence," he said.
Moscow should be using the crisis to its advantage, said Zhirinovsky. "The Russian bear is sleeping instead of using American agression to restore relations with the Arab world."
